findings.title: No re-check after acquiring write lock; concurrent callers all reload the manifest
findings.body: After the read-locked check misses, the code takes the write lock but does not check the cache again. Several goroutines that miss at the same time line up on the lock. Each one then re-reads and re-parses assets-manifest.json, or makes the CDN request, one after another. They also overwrite the cache each time. A double-checked pattern (re-check `entryPointAssetsCache != nil` when not in Dev, after taking `Lock`) would avoid this redundant serialized I/O. In production this happens at startup, or after an earlier failure has left the cache nil.

findings.title: Error result overwrites a previously cached valid value with nil
findings.body: `entryPointAssetsCache = result` runs even when `err != nil`. If a reload fails, the cache is set to nil and the error is returned. This happens in Dev mode on every call, or with a transient file or CDN error. Any good assets cached earlier are lost, and later callers get errors or trigger reloads. Only update the cache when `err == nil`.
